response.title: what do i need to live off solar in a camper for a month
response.answer:
To live off-grid in a camper for 30 days using solar power, you'll need a solar system that can generate enough electricity each day, a battery large enough to last through cloudy weather, and a plan for water, cooking, and waste.

The good news is that you don't need 30 days' worth of battery capacity. Your solar panels recharge your batteries every day.

1. Recommended solar setup

For one or two people living in a camper with a refrigerator, lights, laptops, fans, and occasional appliance use, I'd start with this setup:

SOLAR PANELS

800–1,200W

Power generation

BATTERY STORAGE

5–10 kWh

LiFePO4 batteries

INVERTER

2,000–3,000W

Pure sine wave

SOLAR CONTROLLER

MPPT

Sized for panel and battery voltage

This is a starting point for a moderate-power camper, not a guarantee of unlimited electricity. Air conditioning, electric heating, and cloudy winter conditions can require substantially more capacity.

2. How much electricity will you use?

Here's a realistic example of daily electricity consumption.

Appliance

	

Estimated daily use




12V refrigerator

	

500 Wh




LED lights

	

100 Wh




Laptop (6 hours)

	

360 Wh




Phone charging

	

30 Wh




Ventilation fan

	

200 Wh




Water pump

	

50 Wh




Internet router

	

240 Wh




Miscellaneous / losses

	

300 Wh




Total

	

1,780 Wh/day

That means approximately 1.8 kWh per day, or 54 kWh over 30 days.

With 1,000W of panels and four effective peak-sun-hours, you might generate around 3.2 kWh daily after typical losses. But winter, shade, rain, and roof-mounted panel angles can change this substantially.

3. What solar equipment looks like

Runs standard AC appliances

You'll also need appropriately sized wiring, fuses, disconnects, mounting hardware, and a battery monitor. Have a qualified RV electrical installer size and protect the system. 
Keystone RV
+1

4. Water, cooking, and other essentials

Electricity is only one part of living off-grid for a month.

Requirement

	

Practical solution




Drinking and cooking water

	

3–5 gallons per person daily, including basic washing




Showering

	

Water-saving shower, refillable freshwater tank




Cooking

	

Propane stove or efficient induction cooktop




Food

Toilet

	

RV toilet with dump-station access or suitable alternative




Heating

	

Properly installed vented propane/diesel heater




Internet

	

Cellular hotspot or satellite internet




Emergency power

	

Alternator charging or backup generator

For one person, 3–5 gallons a day means 90–150 gallons over a month. Most campers cannot conveniently carry that much, so plan to refill water and empty waste tanks periodically.

Avoid relying on solar for electric space heating or all-night air conditioning unless you design a much larger system.

5. Estimate your solar needs

Adjust these values to see how much solar and battery capacity your camper might need.

These answers will help determine whether you can get by with a relatively small system or need a much larger one, particularly for air conditioning or winter camping.

To live **off-grid in a camper for 30 days using solar power**, you'll need a solar system that can generate enough electricity each day, a battery large enough to last through cloudy weather, and a plan for water, cooking, and waste.

The good news is that you don't need 30 days' worth of battery capacity. Your solar panels recharge your batteries every day.

## 1. Recommended solar setup

For one or two people living in a camper with a refrigerator, lights, laptops, fans, and occasional appliance use, I'd start with this setup:

<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <grid columns={2} gap={3}>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">SOLAR PANELS</text>
      <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>800–1,200W</title>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Power generation</text>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">BATTERY STORAGE</text>
      <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>5–10 kWh</title>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">LiFePO4 batteries</text>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">INVERTER</text>
      <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>2,000–3,000W</title>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Pure sine wave</text>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">SOLAR CONTROLLER</text>
      <title size="xl" color="default">MPPT</title>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Sized for panel and battery voltage</text>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
</box>

This is a starting point for a moderate-power camper, not a guarantee of unlimited electricity. Air conditioning, electric heating, and cloudy winter conditions can require substantially more capacity.

## 2. How much electricity will you use?

Here's a realistic example of daily electricity consumption.

| Appliance | Estimated daily use |
|---|---:|
| 12V refrigerator | 500 Wh |
| LED lights | 100 Wh |
| Laptop (6 hours) | 360 Wh |
| Phone charging | 30 Wh |
| Ventilation fan | 200 Wh |
| Water pump | 50 Wh |
| Internet router | 240 Wh |
| Miscellaneous / losses | 300 Wh |
| **Total** | **1,780 Wh/day** |

That means approximately **1.8 kWh per day**, or 54 kWh over 30 days.

With 1,000W of panels and four effective peak-sun-hours, you might generate around 3.2 kWh daily after typical losses. But winter, shade, rain, and roof-mounted panel angles can change this substantially. <Cite refs={["turn988431search2","turn988431search5"]}/>

## 3. What solar equipment looks like

<grid columns={2} gap={3}>
  <grid-item>
    <AsyncImage query="RV camper van roof mounted monocrystalline solar panels" aspectRatio="5:4" shop_eligible={true}/>
    **Solar panels**

    <text color="secondary" size="xs">800–1,200W total</text>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <AsyncImage query="LiFePO4 12 volt 200Ah lithium RV battery" aspectRatio="5:4" shop_eligible={true}/>
    **Lithium batteries**

    <text color="secondary" size="xs">5–10 kWh total</text>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <AsyncImage query="Victron MPPT solar charge controller RV" aspectRatio="5:4" shop_eligible={true}/>
    **MPPT controller**

    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Regulates solar charging</text>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <AsyncImage query="pure sine wave power inverter 3000 watt RV" aspectRatio="5:4" shop_eligible={true}/>
    **Power inverter**

    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Runs standard AC appliances</text>
  </grid-item>
</grid>

You'll also need appropriately sized wiring, fuses, disconnects, mounting hardware, and a battery monitor. Have a qualified RV electrical installer size and protect the system. <Cite refs={["turn988431search0","turn988431search9"]}/>

## 4. Water, cooking, and other essentials

Electricity is only one part of living off-grid for a month.

| Requirement | Practical solution |
|---|---|
| Drinking and cooking water | 3–5 gallons per person daily, including basic washing |
| Showering | Water-saving shower, refillable freshwater tank |
| Cooking | Propane stove or efficient induction cooktop |
| Food | 12V compressor refrigerator |
| Toilet | RV toilet with dump-station access or suitable alternative |
| Heating | Properly installed vented propane/diesel heater |
| Internet | Cellular hotspot or satellite internet |
| Emergency power | Alternator charging or backup generator |

For one person, 3–5 gallons a day means **90–150 gallons over a month**. Most campers cannot conveniently carry that much, so plan to refill water and empty waste tanks periodically.

Avoid relying on solar for electric space heating or all-night air conditioning unless you design a much larger system.

## 5. Estimate your solar needs

Adjust these values to see how much solar and battery capacity your camper might need.

{@body const [sun,setSun] = DIL.useState(4)}
{@body const [backup,setBackup] = DIL.useState(2)}
{@body const daily = Number(usage)}
{@body const panels = Math.ceil((daily*1000/(sun*0.8))/100)*100}
{@body const battery = Math.ceil((daily*backup/0.85)*10)/10}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <box gap={1}>
    <label>Daily electricity use</label>
    <radio-group direction="col" value={usage} onChange={setUsage}>

      <radio value="2">Comfortable — 2 kWh/day</radio>
      <radio value="4">Heavy use — 4 kWh/day</radio>
      <radio value="8">Air conditioning / high use — 8 kWh/day</radio>
    </radio-group>
  </box>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row align="center" justify="between">
      <label>Effective peak-sun-hours per day</label>
      **{sun} hours**
    </row>
    <slider min={2} max={7} step={0.5} value={sun} onChange={setSun}/>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row align="center" justify="between">
      <label>Battery backup without sun</label>
      **{backup} days**
    </row>
    <slider min={1} max={4} step={1} value={backup} onChange={setBackup}/>
  </box>
  <divider/>
  <grid columns={2} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs">Estimated solar array</text>
        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{panels.toLocaleString()} W</title>
      </box>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs">Nominal battery capacity</text>
        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{battery.toFixed(1)} kWh</title>
      </box>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <caption>Planning estimates assume 80% solar system efficiency and 85% usable battery capacity. These are energy estimates, not a guarantee of uninterrupted power or inverter compatibility.</caption>
</box>

## 6. Three questions that will determine your actual setup

{@body const [camper,setCamper] = DIL.useState("van")}
{@body const [ac,setAc] = DIL.useState("no")}
{@body const [location,setLocation] = DIL.useState("")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Help me design a 30-day off-grid camper solar setup. Camper type: "+camper+". Air conditioning: "+ac+". Location and season: "+(location||"not decided")+". Recommend equipment, sizing, and approximate budget.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What kind of camper?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={camper} onChange={setCamper}>
        <radio value="van">Camper van</radio>
        <radio value="truck camper">Truck camper</radio>
        <radio value="travel trailer">Travel trailer</radio>
        <radio value="motorhome">Motorhome / RV</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Do you need air conditioning?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={ac} onChange={setAc}>
        <radio value="no">No, just a fan</radio>
        <radio value="a few hours">Yes, a few hours per day</radio>
        <radio value="overnight">Yes, including overnight</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Where and when will you be camping?</label>
      <input value={location} onChange={setLocation} placeholder="e.g. Arizona in January, California in July"/>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Design my solar setup <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>
